dialect.detail: Brazilian Portuguese student exercise, likely compiled with GnuCOBOL; uses DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA with comma as decimal separator in numeric literals (e.g. 0,14; 0,275)

purpose.domain_detail: Brazilian payroll calculation: computes gross salary, INSS (social security) and IRRF (income tax) deductions, and net salary based on hourly rate, hours worked, and number of dependents
purpose.summary: This program accepts employee data (name, ID, hourly rate, hours worked, dependents), calculates gross salary, INSS and IRRF tax deductions using Brazilian tax constants, and displays the resulting payslip breakdown. It is a student exercise demonstrating variables, data entry, arithmetic, and output in COBOL.

notable_features: DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA with comma decimal literals
Brazilian tax constants (INSS 14%, IRRF 27.5%, deductions per dependent)
No PERFORM or GOTO — flat paragraph flow
UTF-8 encoded source with accented characters in AUTHOR
verdict.notes: Program is clearly a student exercise from August 2023 by a Brazilian student (Érica Barbosa). The DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause and comma-decimal literals are characteristic of Brazilian COBOL practice. No PERFORM statements; paragraphs fall through sequentially. Tax rates are simplified/flat-rate approximations, not current Brazilian tax tables.
